subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host provider auth login fail closed before OAuth starts, or should OpenClaw support an authenticated gateway-side credential-forwarding flow?
rationale: The choice defines where sensitive provider OAuth refresh material may be acquired, stored, and transferred across the node/gateway boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent security model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable instruction to run the command on the gateway host while preserving loopback and tunnel workflows.

options.title: Design gateway credential forwarding
options.body: Add an explicit authenticated gateway-side flow for transferring provider auth material instead of consuming tokens into the node-local store.

options.title: Warn but allow local write
options.body: Keep local writes possible with warning copy, accepting the risk that users may still consume refresh credentials on the wrong host.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable instruction to run the command on the gateway host while preserving loopback and tunnel workflows.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the closed same-repo draft for the exact remote-node OAuth guard and have recent related auth-command history.
